baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction أَقْرَبُ ... مِنكُمْ ... لَا تُبْصِرُونَ directly couples comparative nearness with negated visual perception.
baseline_models.mechanism: Spatial or relational distance and perceptual access are decoupled: the nearer party can be immediately present while the more distant observers' eyes do not register it.

activation_trace.role: Nearness as the opposite of distance supplies the comparative spatial or relational arrangement.
Eyesight supplies the denied sensory channel, making invisibility compatible with immediate presence.

changed_reading.before: Nearness would ordinarily make a presence easier for the addressed observers to see.
changed_reading.after: The ayah asserts a presence nearer to the person than the observers are precisely while denying those observers visual access to it.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Negated تُبْصِرُونَ can activate the ب ص ر branch of inward discernment alongside the comparative أَقْرَبُ.
baseline_models.mechanism: Closeness is not sufficient for recognition: a reality may already be intimately available while the addressed group lacks the inward penetration needed to apprehend it.

activation_trace.role: Nearness supplies immediate availability rather than remoteness.
Insight and verified knowledge turn the negation from an optical failure into failed recognition.

changed_reading.before: You do not visually see a nearby presence.
changed_reading.after: You do not penetrate or recognize a reality that is already closer to the person than you are.

context_deltas.mechanism: The concealed record and its restricted contact provide an access-control analogue: something can be present and consequential while remaining enclosed from an unqualified mode of contact. The focus contrast then reads as near reality behind an access boundary, not reality at a great distance.

activation_trace.role: Immediate nearness prevents concealment from being reduced to spatial remoteness.
Inward discernment supplies the unavailable mode of access.
Protective concealment supplies an enclosure that preserves a thing while withholding ordinary access.
Touch by hand supplies the concrete access operation that the sequence restricts.
Purity as removal of defilement supplies the qualification for crossing the access boundary.

structural_cues: The pre-focus sequence places a concealed book immediately beside a statement that only a qualified group touches it.
The focus ayah repeats the same paradoxical geometry: nearness without ordinary access.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies concealment, restricted touch, qualification, and near-but-unperceived presence; I infer one access-boundary pattern across them. A live alternative is that the book sequence and death scene use separate kinds of concealment.

changed_reading.before: The observers simply fail to notice a nearby presence.
changed_reading.after: The observers face a reality that is near but enclosed behind a mode-of-access boundary their present sight does not cross.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding progression fixes the focus at a terminal bodily threshold: something reaches the throat while the companions are actively looking. Nearness therefore becomes operational proximity to the transition itself, whereas human looking reaches only its visible bodily surface.

activation_trace.role: Approaching and coming into immediate contact recasts nearness as involvement at the threshold.
Eyesight is the channel explicitly unable to register the nearer operation.
Arrival at an endpoint supplies the terminal movement into the scene.
The throat as the passage of food and breath locates the endpoint at a bodily conduit.
Directed looking supplies deliberate eyewitness attention, sharpening the contrast with failure to perceive.

structural_cues: 56:83 gives arrival at the throat, 56:84 gives the companions' looking, and 56:85 interrupts that visible scene with a nearer unseen party.
The comparative مِنكُمْ places the nearer party and the human observers around the same person.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies endpoint, throat passage, active looking, and comparative nearness; I infer that the unseen party has operational access to the transition itself. The alternative is purely spatial proximity without an asserted causal role.

changed_reading.before: An unseen party is spatially closer than the visible companions.
changed_reading.after: At the exact bodily threshold the companions watch, the nearer party occupies the operative side of the transition while human sight remains at its exterior.

context_deltas.mechanism: The challenge after the focus converts comparative nearness into a test of effective authority: those who deny being subject to reckoning are invited to reverse the passage, but cannot. The nearer position thus carries jurisdiction over an event the visible companions cannot control.

activation_trace.role: Privileged nearness to authority supplies an ordered relation rather than mere metric distance.
Failure of discernment explains why the addressed group mistakes lack of visible control for lack of governing authority.
Reckoning and recompense supply the jurisdiction explicitly placed in question.
Returning something to its former state supplies the demanded reversal that tests control.
Fulfilling a claim in action makes successful reversal the proof demanded from the challengers.

structural_cues: The two following ayat form a conditional challenge: if the observers are outside judgment, they should return what has reached the throat.
The second-person plural continues the group addressed by مِنكُمْ and لَا تُبْصِرُونَ.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies denied reckoning, a demand for reversal, and a truth test; I infer that the nearer party's proximity entails effective jurisdiction over the transition. Alternatively, the challenge may establish power generally without defining the semantic content of nearness.

changed_reading.before: The comparative describes who is closest to the person.
changed_reading.after: The comparative also distinguishes effective jurisdiction: the unseen nearer party governs the passage that the visible companions cannot reverse.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate reuse of ق ر ب in الْمُقَرَّبِينَ changes nearness from a momentary relation around the dying person into a possible conferred status beyond the threshold. The nearer presence and the brought-near destination-category remain distinct, but the lexical echo makes proximity directional and rank-bearing.

activation_trace.role: Comparative nearness supplies the relation first stated at the threshold.
The favored brought-near group supplies a ranked and conferred form of proximity after the threshold.

structural_cues: After the return challenge, the passage immediately sorts the person into outcomes beginning with الْمُقَرَّبِينَ.
The same root shifts from the active comparison أَقْرَبُ to the passive status مُقَرَّبِينَ.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a comparative q-r-b form followed by a passive brought-near q-r-b category; I infer that threshold nearness foreshadows conferred rank or destination. The live alternative is lexical recurrence without identity between the nearer party and the classified person.

changed_reading.before: Nearness names only the unseen party's position during the death scene.
changed_reading.after: Nearness also opens toward a conferred post-threshold rank: the scene of who is nearer is followed by the possibility of the person being brought near.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing assertion of reality and settled knowledge prevents لَا تُبْصِرُونَ from functioning as an epistemic veto. Sensory nonappearance marks a limit of the observers' present mode, while the event is framed as fixed reality and certainty.

activation_trace.role: Denied eyesight supplies the limited evidentiary mode whose failure is being contained.
Insight supplies a broader apprehension not exhausted by immediate optical evidence.
Reality fixed against falsehood supplies the ontic status unaffected by nonappearance.
Stable knowledge with doubt removed supplies the epistemic endpoint beyond present sight.

structural_cues: The passage closes its outcome sequence with حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ after the earlier denial of visual perception.
The demonstrative هَٰذَا gathers the narrated transition and outcomes as the object of the certainty claim.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies sensory denial followed by fixed reality and doubtless knowledge; I infer that the perception gap is mode-specific rather than evidence of absence. Alternatively, the closing certainty may confirm the whole outcome sequence without targeting 56:85 in particular.

changed_reading.before: What the observers cannot see remains epistemically inaccessible.
changed_reading.after: Their inability to see identifies a bounded sensory mode; it does not diminish the passage's claim that the unseen transition is fixed reality.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the birth-nearness branch of ق ر ب and the fetus branch of ج ن ن across surfaces that ordinarily denote comparative nearness and a garden. It remains anchored in أَقْرَبُ and in the packet's throat-to-spirit sequence, which together support a threshold analogy. Downstream prose should present it only as an exploratory inverse-birth image, not as the lexical meaning of the ayah or of جَنَّة.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus أَقْرَبُ can activate nearness of birth, while the immediately surrounding sequence locates a life-ending passage at the throat.

activation_trace.role: Nearness of birth turns comparative closeness into imminence at a bodily passage.
The throat as food-and-breath conduit supplies the bodily threshold for the inverse-birth analogy.
Spirit or life supplies what can be imagined as emerging through the terminal threshold.
The hidden fetus branch supplies the cross-domain image of emergence from one enclosed mode into another.

changed_reading.before: The nearer unseen presence attends an ending that the companions cannot perceive.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the ending can be imaged as an inverse birth: life crosses a throat-threshold into a hidden mode while the nearer presence attends the passage.

strongest_changes: The throat-and-looking sequence revises generic nearness into operational access at a terminal bodily threshold.
The return challenge recasts nearness as effective jurisdiction that visible companions cannot match.
The later مُقَرَّبِينَ echo extends nearness from threshold position toward conferred rank.
حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ makes failed eyesight a bounded mode of access rather than evidence of absence.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah becomes a hinge between two access regimes: companions can look at the visible body but cannot reach the nearer operation, while the passage moves from concealed text through a concealed transition to classified outcomes and certainty.
remaining_uncertainties: The comparative nearness may be spatial, relational, operational, or several of these at once.
The concealed-book sequence may genuinely prime the death scene's access boundary or may remain only a useful structural analogy.
The link from أَقْرَبُ to مُقَرَّبِينَ is lexically strong but does not by itself identify the nearer party with the brought-near person.
The inverse-birth model depends on branch-distant activation and should remain exploratory.
